## Summary of Findings 1:  **HUGE** partisan conflict effects {background-image="https://i.pinimg.com/originals/53/88/62/538862d56741248fc085109b93946efb.png" background-opacity=".1"}

Officials reporting **high** partisan conflict over their agencies

- More perceived influence of appointees
- Less perceived influence of career staff

## Summary of Findings 2:  **CONDITIONAL** partisan conflict effects {background-image="https://i.pinimg.com/originals/53/88/62/538862d56741248fc085109b93946efb.png" background-opacity=".1"}

Officials reporting **high** partisan conflict over **liberal agencies**

- More perceived influence of appointees

Officials reporting **low** partisan conflict over **conservative agencies** 

- More perceived influence of career staff

. . .

[Does this depend on who the president is? ]()

## Summary of Findings 3: {background-image="https://i.pinimg.com/originals/53/88/62/538862d56741248fc085109b93946efb.png" background-opacity=".1"}

### Insulated agencies 

- Less perceived influence of president/OMB/OIRA

### Expertise + uncertainty 

- Less perceived influence of appointees, Congress, the president, and OMB/OIRA when their agency's work requires skill and policy effects are uncertain

## Thoughts on Analysis {.incremental background-image="https://i.pinimg.com/originals/53/88/62/538862d56741248fc085109b93946efb.png" background-opacity=".1"}

More direct tests of ***relative*** perceived influence 

- [Pairwise ratios or normalized 'influence budget']()

. . .

More descriptives by agency and type of official

- [Are those reporting conflict the ones we would expect? ]()
- [Are people more likely to see others as having power? ]()
- [Are perceptions formed by official duties? ]()
- [Recent orders or attention from the president or Congress? ]()

Descriptively leverage sub-agency heterogeneity.

## If we do this survey again

- Ask about regulated industry influence! 
- Require responses to add up to 100

- Disaggregate career: "legal experts" vs "substantive experts" 


## Smaller notes

<!--
- Predicted probabilities rather than marginal effects for Figure 3 since the theory is about the joint effect, not the conditional marginal effect of difficulty. 


- Results as presented are too complex and difficult to follow. --> 

- Many agencies were dropped when you filtered to rulemaking; who is left? 

- Careful how you talk about the model---it is not a diff-in-diff---not "moving from high conflict to low conflict" but rather "comparing high-conflict and low-conflict." 

## From discussion 

Unified agenda is problematic. 

- may not be about content, rather signaling to principals that they are working on it

Sources of external agenda influence: 

- OIRA prompt letters 
- petitions 

Insulation 

- Use Jen's disaggregated measures
